chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, that the two (Imams) said:
Do not wash your garment from the urine of an animal whose flesh is eaten.
ai.seo_question: Do I need to wash my clothes if an animal whose meat is halal urinates on them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of inherent purity (asl al-taharah) for the urine of halal animals, such as cows and sheep, distinguishing them from impure creatures. It reflects the Shia juristic view that minor impurities (kathir al-ma') from edible animals do not necessitate washing the garment for prayer, provided the substance is removed, thereby easing ritual obligations for the faithful.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara,
Both, (5<sup>th</sup> and 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) said: ‘There is no need to wash your clothes from the urine of something that you can eat - its flesh’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “The two Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, have said, ‘
It is not necessary for you to wash your clothes because of urine of the edible animals.’”
